maria-support: Hey team — customer on Private/VPC (subnet eu-west-1a) reporting intermittent stream resets and TLS handshake failures when calling our inference endpoint behind their NAT. ~10% of requests fail during bursts, affects streaming only. Ticket #12345. Can someone triage?

raj-infra: On it. Do we have tcpdump/traceroute snippets or the VPC/NACL/SG IDs? Any pattern on source/dest ports?

maria-support: They attached a tcpdump excerpt showing initial SYN to 443 then RST from our side IP (their NAT EIP). They also provided NACL/SG IDs: nl-0a1b2c3d, sg-0f1e2d3c. Snippet from tcpdump: ```15:22:11.123456 IP 10.0.2.15.52345 > 3.120.45.67.443: Flags [S], seq 0
15:22:11.234567 IP 3.120.45.67.443 > 10.0.2.15.52345: Flags [R], seq 1
```

alex-sre: Quick hypothesis: stateless NACL has an explicit DENY for ephemeral destination ports, which will drop the return packets even though SG is stateful. Can you paste the NACL rules? Rule ordering matters (lowest number evaluated first).

maria-support: Here are the NACL rules they sent (ordered):
```
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 0.0.0.0/0 443
Rule 110: DENY TCP 0.0.0.0/0 32768-65535
Rule 120: ALLOW ALL 0.0.0.0/0
```

alex-sre: Yep, that's it. Because NACLs are evaluated by rule number ascending, a DENY at 110 will match and drop packets to ephemeral ports before the catch-all allow at 120. Client outbound uses source ephemeral port -> destination 443 allowed, but return has source 443 dest ephemeral (32768+), which hits the DENY. Explains intermittent failures (depends on random ephemeral port chosen).

sam-eng: Additional checks: confirm they're SNATing via NAT gateway — SNAT changes source to NAT EIP and uses ephemeral ports on the NAT for return mapping. If ephemeral range overlaps DENY, return resets happen. Also check if any other NACLs on the path have similar denies.

maria-support: Customer confirmed NAT gateway in front of their subnet. They made a quick change: inserted ALLOW TCP 32768-65535 at rule 105 (so it evaluates before the DENY).

raj-infra: Nice workaround. Can they instead remove the DENY or narrow it? Best practice is allow required ephemeral range (1024-65535) or rely on explicit allow rules with no deny unless intended for strict lockdown.

maria-support: After the quick change, they report error rate dropped to 0% in 45 minutes and streaming stabilized.

alex-sre: Resolution: NACL rule ordering caused ephemeral return ports to be dropped. Remediation options: (1) Add ALLOW ephemeral rule with lower rule number than any DENY that would match, (2) delete the DENY rule if not required, or (3) move deny to a higher-numbered rule after explicit ephemeral allow. Also note to check for stateful SG assumptions vs stateless NACLs in our docs.

sam-eng: I'll add a short blurb to the VPC onboarding runbook: "If using Private inference, ensure NACLs do not deny ephemeral return port ranges used by NAT gateways (typ. 32768-65535 on Linux, 1024-65535 older systems)."

maria-support: Customer happy and closing the ticket. They've asked for a short explanation to share with their network team — pasted suggested wording and screenshots.

alex-sre: Assigning follow-up: update docs + add automated check in our private deployment checklist to validate NACLs for ephemeral ranges.

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-7893 to track runbook update and checklist check. :white_check_mark: 

maria-support: thanks all :pray: marking as resolved on our side, will keep an eye if anything resurfaces.
